subject: Biotechnology
title: Silk and Dyes from Nature
description: A 60-second lesson on Silk and Dyes from Nature.

hook.text: Chinese silk production dates back 5,000 years — silkworms were the first biotech factories for materials.

buildup.text: Each silkworm produces a single thread up to 900 meters long — spun from liquid protein in its glands.

discovery.text: Indigo dye came from plant fermentation — bacteria in the vat converted plant compounds to blue pigment.

twist.text: Synthetic indigo replaced bio-indigo in the 1900s — but now biotech is engineering bacteria to make it again.

climax.text: Spider silk genes in goats, bacteria, and yeast produce fibers stronger than steel — bio-materials return.

punchline.text: Ancient biomaterials inspired modern biotech — the circle closes.

quiz.question: Why is biotechnology being used to produce indigo dye again?
options: Synthetic indigo is no longer available
Bio-based indigo can be more sustainable than chemical synthesis
Plants no longer grow indigo-producing compounds
